text: Gödel's First Incompleteness Theorem says that for any consistent, effectively axiomatizable theory T extending arithmetic:
choices: T can prove its own consistency
every arithmetic truth is provable in T
there is a sentence G_T with T ⊬ G_T and T ⊬ ¬G_T, yet G_T is true in ℕ
explanation: The First Theorem produces the Gödel sentence G_T ('I am not provable in T'), which is neither provable nor refutable in T though true in the standard model ℕ. Option C is exactly what incompleteness denies; option A is the (false) content ruled out by the Second Theorem; option B contradicts the consistency hypothesis.
